content: Partner 1 asked to dissolve and divide a property purchased under community, but the separation authorization pre‑dated the 2015 reform moving dissolution to the presidential order. The issue was admissibility when final separation had not been proven under the prior rule (ex nunc at final judgment). The court framed dissolution as a condition of action existing at the time of decision, not filing, yet required proof the separation judgment had become final. Principles: in cases governed by pre‑2015 law, dissolution arises at finality; absent proof, the division claim is inadmissible. Costs compensated due to novelty of the question. 1.
